Suggestion: keep `pre-commit-checks` on `self-hosted` and leave the rest of the routing as it is.

The split looks right otherwise. The integration-test chain (`build-itest-binaries` on `rith-cdk-large` plus the six itest jobs) stays entirely on Rith, so the archive and harness binaries come from the run cache, fork PRs included. The `deps-ci` chain (`quick-check`, clippy/tests, examples, docs) stays entirely on cdk-infra. `rusqlite-compat` and `discover_ci_groups` share no build outputs, so either pool is fine for them.

`pre-commit-checks` is different:

1. **It gates almost the whole run.** Nearly every job, including all the cdk-infra jobs, `needs:` it. On Rith, a Rith outage or full queue holds up CI work that doesn't need Rith at all.
2. **It builds the `.#stable` dev shell.** `fuzz-check`, the postgres/supabase/redis tests and the FFI/binding jobs use the same shell on cdk-infra. Usually it's already in Attic from `main`. When a PR changes `flake.lock` or the toolchain, though, the shell is built on Rith, published only to that run's cache, and built again on cdk-infra, which the Rith run cache can't serve.

```diff
   pre-commit-checks:
-    runs-on: rith-cdk
+    runs-on: self-hosted
```

https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/pull/2861, https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/pull/2863, https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/pull/2864 all merged, which landed much of the work outside of the actual spec change for BLS.

Thanks for this @SovereignTechnology . I have confirmed both points on the current main branch and i would like to pick this up. i would highlight my approach below:

1. **Fee defaults: fixed the docs and left the code as is.**
`default_ldk_fee_percent() = 0.04` and `default_ldk_reserve_fee_min() = 4` have been the defaults since the LDK Node backend was added (#904). It was the example comments that were wrong; they look copied from the `[cln]`/`[lnd]` sections. Changing the defaults instead would silently lower the fee reserve for every existing ldk-node mint that relies on them, so the PR corrects the comments in `example.config.toml` to 4% / 4 sats. If maintainers would prefer matching CLN/LND (0.02 / 2), I think that should be a separate, explicitly announced change.

2. **`gossip_source_type` now controls the gossip source.**
Previously the field was parsed but never used: setup picked RGS purely based on whether `rgs_url` was set. Now:
- not set: unchanged: RGS if `rgs_url` is set, otherwise P2P
- `p2p`: always P2P; a warning is logged if `rgs_url` is also set
- `rgs`: RGS; startup fails if `rgs_url` is missing
- any other value: startup error naming the value

Matching ignores case, the same as `bitcoin_network`. Configs that don't set the field behave exactly as before. The two behaviour changes (`p2p` now overrides `rgs_url`, and `rgs` without a URL now fails instead of silently using P2P) are noted in the CHANGELOG.

3. **Duplicate key removed.** `example.config.toml` defined `gossip_source_type` twice in `[ldk_node]`, so uncommenting the whole block failed TOML parsing. There is now a single entry, with a short explanation of the options.

Thanks for picking up #2848. Removing RGS settles the mismatch more cleanly than honouring the setting would have.

One thing from reading the diff (not from running it): the "Ignoring removed configuration field" warning looks like it is only visible on `config init`.

- `deserialize_configuration` emits it with `tracing::warn!`, but the only subscribers are installed in `setup_tracing` and in the `config init` arm of `main.rs`.
- On daemon start, `run_mintd_from_database` calls `service.startup()` (which parses the stored document) before `setup_tracing`, so the warning is dropped.
- `config validate`, `config apply` and `config migrate` install no subscriber at all. `config migrate` also re-serializes the settings, so the two fields disappear from the migrated file with no notice.

So a mint whose stored config has `gossip_source_type = "rgs"` and an `rgs_url` switches to P2P on upgrade without the operator seeing anything. If that matters, collecting the ignored fields in `deserialize_configuration` and reporting them after tracing is up (and printing them from the `config` subcommands) would cover it.

Related and smaller: `CDK_MINTD_LDK_NODE_RGS_URL` and `CDK_MINTD_LDK_NODE_GOSSIP_SOURCE_TYPE` are now ignored silently, and the old README and NETWORK_GUIDE Docker examples set exactly those. A one-line warning when either is present, or a REMOVED entry in the changelog, would help people who copied them.

Happy to send a small follow-up for either if it's useful.

One remaining correction in `RemovePendingProofs::execute`: please make restoration conditional on the row still being `Pending` and owned by this receive at the time of the database write.

The new `held_ys` filter handles the crash-before-overwrite recovery case, but the live path supplies every original input Y when it registers compensation. That list does not establish current ownership. For example, while receive is awaiting a definitive swap rejection, a concurrent send-status check can remove a now-spent input and finish the send saga. Compensation then recreates the saved `PendingSpent` row, pointing at the deleted send saga. This stale-row resurrection is introduced by restoring the snapshots.

The current wallet database trait cannot express the conditional write: `update_proofs` is unconditional, and `release_proofs` only releases to `Unspent`. A focused backend operation for receive compensation could restore/remove only rows whose current owner matches the receive saga and whose state is `Pending`, checking those conditions atomically with the mutation. A separate read before `update_proofs` would still leave a race.

Please add a deterministic regression that pauses the live receive before returning a definitive rejection, removes or marks its input spent, and verifies compensation does not recreate or overwrite it. The broader pre-existing race between concurrent receives can remain a separate follow-up.

I added `restore_pending_proofs` to the wallet database trait: it only overwrites or deletes rows that are still Pending and owned by the receive, checked in the same write (one transaction in SQL and redb, a filtered write per row in Supabase). `RemovePendingProofs` now goes through it (6e28394, 991820a). 56923e8 adds the regression: it pauses the live receive inside the swap, removes or marks the input spent, then returns a definitive rejection and checks the row isn't recreated or overwritten. It fails on the previous head.

This should probably wait for #2964 (remove `Clone` from `Mint`). This PR spawns the swap with `self.clone()`, which won't compile once that lands. After #2964 merges, I'll rebase and switch `process_swap_request` to `self: &Arc<Self>` with `Arc::clone(self)`, the same pattern #2964 uses for `melt` and `start`. I've already tested that version on top of #2964: clippy is clean, the `cdk` lib tests pass, and `test_swap_flow` passes.

Keeping the rest of the batch when one payment check fails makes sense. Could you also guard against the fallback sending an older state for the quote whose check failed? The backfill can read `UNPAID`, then the subscriber can receive a live `PAID` while the backend check is pending. If the check fails, this change sends the saved `UNPAID` snapshot, leaving the wallet one state behind.

Before merging, I'd like a regression test that holds the check open, delivers `PAID` to the subscriber, then releases the check with an error. The subscriber should still receive the other quote's initial state and should never receive `UNPAID` after `PAID` for the first quote.

The shared ordering fix can live in #2989. If it lands first and covers this sequence, rebasing this PR onto it would address my concern.
